title: postMessage, structured clone, and transferables
hook: postMessage copies most data via the structured clone algorithm — expensive for large ArrayBuffers. Transferables move ownership zero-copy: after transfer, the sender's buffer is detached and unusable.

blocks.text: **Structured clone**: recursive copy of supported types (objects, arrays, Map, Date, ArrayBuffer copy). **Transfer list**: second argument `[buffer]` **moves** ArrayBuffer, MessagePort, ImageBitmap — sender loses access. **Clone vs transfer**: clone duplicates memory; transfer reassigns ownership without copy.

entries.plainDefinition: Deep copy for postMessage and indexedDB.
Object that can move between contexts without copy.

blocks.text: Sending 50MB image bitmap to Worker via clone doubles memory briefly — transfer avoids copy. Forgetting transfer list on large TypedArray-backed buffers causes GC pressure and jank. MessageChannel ports transfer for bidirectional pipes.

blocks.title: Functions not cloneable
blocks.body: postMessage cannot send functions or DOM nodes — only structured-cloneable types.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Cloning multi-MB buffers. Using buffer after transfer. Sending non-cloneable functions.

blocks.text: Serialization cost dominates small messages — batch work per postMessage. Comlink library abstracts RPC over postMessage. In Node worker_threads, transfer list same semantics. Benchmark clone vs transfer for image processing pipeline.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Clones 100MB and wonders why slow. Uses buffer after transfer. Thinks postMessage shares object reference.

interviewTakeaways: Transfer list moves ArrayBuffer — sender detached.
60s: postMessage clones by default. Transfer [buffer] for zero-copy — byteLength 0 on sender. MessagePort transferable. SharedArrayBuffer different — shared memory.
